title: High level of deforestation continues
titleChinese: 大规模森林砍伐活动仍在继续
paragraphs: We are all aware of the threats our planet is facing. Experts agree that it’s mainly us humans who are responsible for the destruction of the environment. Activities such as mass farming and burning fossil fuels are taking their toll on our climate – and we’re suffering too through natural disasters such as flooding and more frequent droughts.

One of the most destructive activities we are carrying out is cutting down forests - deforestation. This is done for many reasons, such as providing wood for fuel, making land available for housing or for creating space for more cattle to graze on. This has been most noticeable in Brazil, which is home to the world’s largest rainforest. Deforestation there has hit its highest rate in a decade, according to official data. Over the course of a year, an area about five times the size of London has been destroyed.

The amount of deforestation in the Amazon and in other tropical regions has actually seen a decline but the figures are still large. Global Forest Watch say that in 2018, an area equivalent to 30 football fields were cut down every minute. Frances Seymour from the World Resources Institute says that “If you look back over the last 18 years, it is clear that the overall trend is still upwards. We are nowhere near winning this battle."

What’s special about places like the Amazon is that they are primary forests which exist in their original condition with some species of trees dating back thousands of years. This habitat is home to unique and rare animals and is critical for sustaining biodiversity. The BBC’s environment correspondent, Matt McGrath, says “These old forests really matter as stores of carbon dioxide, which is why the loss of 3.6 million hectares in 2018 is concerning.”

Brazil has taken some steps to try and decrease deforestation by introducing government policies including fines for breaking land use regulations and clamping down on illegal logging. And International campaigns to stop the trade of soy and beef farmed on deforested parts of the Amazon have also had a significant impact. But meanwhile other parts of the world, such as Ghana and the Democratic Republic of Congo, are seeing dramatic increases. So it seems only political will and human conscience will tackle this problem and save planet Earth.

vocabulary.entry: mass farming /mæs ˈfɑːmɪŋ/ 大规模农业耕作
vocabulary.example: Mass farming has greatly increased food production but also caused environmental problems.
vocabulary.translation: 大规模农业耕作大幅提高了粮食产量，但也引发了诸多环境问题。

vocabulary.entry: fossil fuel /ˈfɒsl fjuːəl/ 化石燃料
vocabulary.example: Coal, oil and natural gas are all common fossil fuels.
vocabulary.translation: 煤炭、石油和天然气都是常见的化石燃料。

vocabulary.entry: take their toll on /teɪk ðeə təʊl ɒn/ 对……造成损害；产生负面影响
vocabulary.example: Years of hard work have taken their toll on his health.
vocabulary.translation: 多年的辛劳工作损害了他的健康。

vocabulary.entry: drought /draʊt/ n. 干旱；旱灾
vocabulary.example: The region is suffering from a severe drought that has lasted for months.
vocabulary.translation: 该地区正遭受持续数月的严重干旱。

vocabulary.entry: deforestation /ˌdiːˌfɒrɪˈsteɪʃn/ n. 砍伐森林；毁林
vocabulary.example: Deforestation is one of the main causes of global warming.
vocabulary.translation: 砍伐森林是造成全球变暖的主要原因之一。

vocabulary.entry: graze on /ɡreɪz ɒn/ （动物）吃草；啃食
vocabulary.example: Sheep and cattle graze on the grassland all year round.
vocabulary.translation: 牛羊整年都在这片草原上吃草。

vocabulary.entry: tropical region /ˈtrɒpɪkl ˈriːdʒən/ 热带地区
vocabulary.example: Rice and sugarcane are widely grown in tropical regions.
vocabulary.translation: 水稻和甘蔗在热带地区被广泛种植。

vocabulary.entry: equivalent to /ɪˈkwɪvələnt tu/ 等同于；相当于
vocabulary.example: The price of the watch is equivalent to a month's salary of mine.
vocabulary.translation: 这块手表的价格相当于我一个月的工资。

vocabulary.entry: overall trend /ˌəʊvərˈɔːl trend/ 总体趋势
vocabulary.example: The overall trend of the stock market is upward this year.
vocabulary.translation: 今年股市的总体趋势是上涨的。

vocabulary.entry: nowhere near /ˈnəʊweə nɪə/ 远不及；完全不
vocabulary.example: We are nowhere near finishing the project before the deadline.
vocabulary.translation: 我们远无法在截止日期前完成这个项目。

vocabulary.entry: primary forest /ˈpraɪməri ˈfɒrɪst/ 原生林；原始森林
vocabulary.example: Primary forests are rich in biodiversity and should be well protected.
vocabulary.translation: 原生林生物多样性丰富，应当得到妥善保护。

vocabulary.entry: habitat /ˈhæbɪtæt/ n. 栖息地；生活环境
vocabulary.example: The destruction of natural habitats threatens many wild animals.
vocabulary.translation: 自然栖息地的破坏威胁着许多野生动物的生存。

vocabulary.entry: sustain biodiversity /səˈsteɪn ˌbaɪəʊdaɪˈvɜːsəti/ 维护生物多样性
vocabulary.example: Protecting wetlands is an effective way to sustain biodiversity.
vocabulary.translation: 保护湿地是维护生物多样性的有效途径。

vocabulary.entry: correspondent /ˌkɒrəˈspɒndənt/ n. 通讯员；记者
vocabulary.example: She works as a foreign correspondent for a national newspaper.
vocabulary.translation: 她是一家全国性报纸的驻外记者。

vocabulary.entry: store /stɔː(r)/ n. 储存库；储备
vocabulary.example: Oceans are important stores of carbon in the Earth's ecosystem.
vocabulary.translation: 海洋是地球生态系统中重要的碳储存库。

vocabulary.entry: hectare /ˈhekteə(r)/ n. 公顷
vocabulary.example: The new park covers an area of 50 hectares.
vocabulary.translation: 这座新公园占地面积为50公顷。

vocabulary.entry: land use regulation /lænd juːz ˌreɡjuˈleɪʃn/ 土地使用规定
vocabulary.example: The government has revised the land use regulation to protect farmland.
vocabulary.translation: 政府修订了土地使用规定，以保护农田。

vocabulary.entry: clamp down on /klæmp daʊn ɒn/ 严厉打击；严格管控
vocabulary.example: The police are clamping down on illegal parking in the city center.
vocabulary.translation: 警方正在严厉打击市中心的违章停车行为。

vocabulary.entry: illegal logging /ɪˈliːɡl ˈlɒɡɪŋ/ 非法伐木
vocabulary.example: The local government has taken measures to stop illegal logging in the mountains.
vocabulary.translation: 当地政府已经采取措施，制止山区的非法伐木行为。

vocabulary.entry: campaign /kæmˈpeɪn/ n. 运动；活动
vocabulary.example: The charity launched a campaign to help homeless people.
vocabulary.translation: 这家慈善机构发起了一场帮助无家可归者的活动。

vocabulary.entry: dramatic increase /drəˈmætɪk ˈɪŋkriːs/ 急剧增长；大幅上升
vocabulary.example: There has been a dramatic increase in the number of tourists this year.
vocabulary.translation: 今年游客的数量出现了急剧增长。

vocabulary.entry: political will /pəˈlɪtɪkl wɪl/ 政治决心；政治意愿
vocabulary.example: Strong political will is needed to solve the problem of climate change.
vocabulary.translation: 解决气候变化问题需要坚定的政治决心。

sentences.english: We are all aware of the threats our planet is facing.
sentences.chinese: 我们都清楚地球正面临着怎样的威胁。

sentences.english: Experts agree that it’s mainly us humans who are responsible for the destruction of the environment.
sentences.chinese: 专家们一致认为，环境遭到破坏，主要责任在我们人类。

sentences.english: Activities such as mass farming and burning fossil fuels are taking their toll on our climate – and we’re suffering too through natural disasters such as flooding and more frequent droughts.
sentences.chinese: 大规模农业耕作、燃烧化石燃料这类活动正在给气候造成严重损害，而我们也正承受着自然灾害带来的后果——洪水和愈发频繁的干旱。

sentences.english: One of the most destructive activities we are carrying out is cutting down forests - deforestation.
sentences.chinese: 人类正在进行的最具破坏性的活动之一就是砍伐森林。

sentences.english: This is done for many reasons, such as providing wood for fuel, making land available for housing or for creating space for more cattle to graze on.
sentences.chinese: 人们这么做的原因有很多，比如获取木材当燃料、腾出土地建造房屋，或是开辟更多空间让牛群吃草。

sentences.english: This has been most noticeable in Brazil, which is home to the world’s largest rainforest.
sentences.chinese: 这一现象在巴西表现得尤为明显，因为这里有着全球最大的热带雨林。

sentences.english: Deforestation there has hit its highest rate in a decade, according to official data.
sentences.chinese: 官方数据显示，巴西的森林砍伐率已经达到了十年来的最高值。

sentences.english: Over the course of a year, an area about five times the size of London has been destroyed.
sentences.chinese: 在一年的时间里，大约五个伦敦面积大小的森林遭到了破坏。

sentences.english: The amount of deforestation in the Amazon and in other tropical regions has actually seen a decline but the figures are still large.
sentences.chinese: 亚马逊流域以及其他热带地区的森林砍伐量实际上已经有所下降，但总量依然不容小觑。

sentences.english: Global Forest Watch say that in 2018, an area equivalent to 30 football fields were cut down every minute.
sentences.chinese: 全球森林观察组织称，2018年，每分钟就有相当于30个足球场面积的森林被砍伐。

sentences.english: Frances Seymour from the World Resources Institute says that “If you look back over the last 18 years, it is clear that the overall trend is still upwards.
sentences.chinese: 世界资源研究所的弗朗西斯·西摩表示：“回顾过去18年的情况，很明显整体趋势仍在恶化。

sentences.english: We are nowhere near winning this battle."
sentences.chinese: 我们远未打赢这场战役。”

sentences.english: What’s special about places like the Amazon is that they are primary forests which exist in their original condition with some species of trees dating back thousands of years.
sentences.chinese: 像亚马逊这样的地区有着独特之处，它们属于原生林，保持着原始的生态状态，其中一些树种的历史可以追溯到数千年以前。

sentences.english: This habitat is home to unique and rare animals and is critical for sustaining biodiversity.
sentences.chinese: 这片栖息地是珍稀特有动物的家园，对维护生物多样性至关重要。

sentences.english: The BBC’s environment correspondent, Matt McGrath, says “These old forests really matter as stores of carbon dioxide, which is why the loss of 3.6 million hectares in 2018 is concerning.”
sentences.chinese: 英国广播公司环境记者马特·麦格拉思表示：“这些古老的森林作为二氧化碳的储存库，有着不可替代的作用，这也是为什么2018年失去360万公顷森林的消息会引发担忧。”

sentences.english: Brazil has taken some steps to try and decrease deforestation by introducing government policies including fines for breaking land use regulations and clamping down on illegal logging.
sentences.chinese: 巴西已经采取了一些措施来减少森林砍伐，出台了多项政府政策，包括对违反土地使用规定的行为处以罚款，以及严厉打击非法伐木行为。

sentences.english: And International campaigns to stop the trade of soy and beef farmed on deforested parts of the Amazon have also had a significant impact.
sentences.chinese: 此外，国际社会发起了相关运动，禁止交易产自亚马逊毁林区的大豆和牛肉，这些举措也产生了显著的影响。

sentences.english: But meanwhile other parts of the world, such as Ghana and the Democratic Republic of Congo, are seeing dramatic increases.
sentences.chinese: 但与此同时，世界上其他地区，比如加纳和刚果民主共和国，森林砍伐现象正急剧增多。

sentences.english: So it seems only political will and human conscience will tackle this problem and save planet Earth.
sentences.chinese: 如此看来，或许只有凭借政治决心和人类良知，才能解决这个问题，拯救我们的地球家园。
